zh: 明元郭皇后，西平人也，世河右大族。
literal: Empress Ming-Yuan of the Guo clan was a native of Xiping and for generations a great clan west of the Yellow River.
idiomatic: Empress Ming-Yuan of the Guo clan came from Xiping; her family was a great house west of the Yellow River for generations.

zh: 黃初中，本郡反叛，遂沒入宮。
literal: In the Huangchu era the commandery rebelled, and she was then taken into the palace.
idiomatic: During Huangchu her commandery rebelled, and she was taken into the palace.

zh: 明帝即位，甚見愛幸，拜為夫人。
literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne she was greatly favored and invested as Lady.
idiomatic: Once Ming-di succeeded she won great favor and was made Lady.

zh: 叔父立為騎都尉，從父芝為虎賁中郎將。
literal: Her father's younger brother Li was appointed Cavalry Commandant; her father's cousin Zhi was made Colonel of the Tiger Guards.
idiomatic: Her uncle Li became cavalry commandant and her father's cousin Guo Zhi colonel of the tiger guards.

literal: When the emperor was gravely ill she was then established as empress.
idiomatic: When the emperor fell gravely ill she was enthroned as empress.

zh: 齊王即位，尊后為皇太后，稱永寧宮，追封諡太后父滿為西都定侯，以立子建紹其爵。
literal: When the Prince of Qi ascended the throne he honored her as Empress Dowager, with her residence called Yongning Palace; he posthumously enfeoffed and honored the empress dowager's father Man as Marquis Ding of Xidu, and had his son Jian continue his noble rank.
idiomatic: When Cao Fang succeeded he raised her to Empress Dowager of Yongning Palace, posthumously ennobled her father Man as Marquis Ding of Xidu, and had his son Jian inherit the title.

literal: The empress dowager's mother Du was enfeoffed as Mistress of Heyang.
idiomatic: Her mother Du was enfeoffed as lady of Heyang.

zh: 芝遷散騎常侍、長水校尉，《魏略》曰：諸郭之中，芝最壯直。
literal: Zhi was transferred to Regular Palace Attendant and Colonel of the Changshui Guard; the Wei Summary states: Among all the Guo clan, Zhi was the most forceful and upright.
idiomatic: Guo Zhi was promoted to regular palace attendant and colonel of the Changshui guard. The Wei Summary says that among the Guo clan Zhi was the most forceful and upright.

literal: Earlier he had on other merit been enfeoffed as marquis.
idiomatic: He had earlier been enfeoffed as marquis on other merits.

literal: Li was made General Who Displays Virtue; both were enfeoffed as full marquises.
idiomatic: Li was made general who displays virtue; both were enfeoffed as full marquises.

literal: Jian's elder brother De had been given out in adoption to the Zhen clan.
idiomatic: Jian's elder brother De had been given in adoption to the Zhen clan.

zh: 德及建俱為鎮護將軍，皆封列侯，並掌宿衛。
literal: De and Jian were both made Generals Who Guard the Garrisons, all enfeoffed as full marquises, and together held command of the palace guard.
idiomatic: De and Jian both became generals who guard the garrisons, were enfeoffed as full marquises, and jointly commanded the palace guard.

zh: 值三主幼弱，宰輔統政，與奪大事，皆先諮啟於太后而後施行。
literal: It happened that three rulers were young and weak and chief ministers held unified government; in granting and taking away great affairs all first consulted and reported to the empress dowager and only then were carried out.
idiomatic: With three successive child emperors and regents holding power, every major appointment or dismissal was first reported to the empress dowager before it was enacted.

zh: 毌丘儉、鍾會等作亂，咸假其命而以為辭焉。
literal: When Guanqiu Jian, Zhong Hui, and others raised rebellion, they all borrowed her command and used it as their pretext.
idiomatic: When Guanqiu Jian, Zhong Hui, and others rebelled, they all invoked her authority as their pretext.

zh: 景元四年十二日崩，五年二月，葬高平陵西。
literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Jingyuan she died; in the second month of the fifth year she was buried west of Gaoping Mausoleum.
idiomatic: She died in the twelfth month of Jingyuan 4 and was buried west of Gaoping Mausoleum in the second month of the following year.

zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰：建字叔始，有器局而強問，泰始中疾薨。
literal: Commendations of the Lords of Jin states: Jian, courtesy name Shushi, had capacity and breadth of vision and was forceful in inquiry; in the Taishi era he died of illness.
idiomatic: Commendations of the Lords of Jin records that Jian, styled Shushi, had breadth of vision and forceful judgment; he died of illness during Taishi.

literal: His son Gu succeeded and served as Supervisor in Attendance.
idiomatic: His son Gu succeeded him and served as supervisor in attendance.
